questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to stop toddlers having tantrums
Why toddlers need more sleep than adults
What adults can learn from toddlers' self-talk
How toddlers learn to walk and dress themselves
questions.why: They ask what adults can learn from toddlers, and the answer is positive self-talk.

questions.q: Why do toddlers often have tantrums, according to Neil?
options: They feel frustrated when they can't do what they want
They are usually tired or hungry
They are copying the angry behaviour of the adults around them
They want to be left alone
questions.why: He says when toddlers can't do the things they want, their frustration leads to tantrums.

questions.q: Why does Neil say it seems strange that adults could learn from toddlers?
options: Because toddlers can't talk yet
Because adults are too busy to watch them
Because toddlers are always angry
Because toddlers depend on their parents
questions.why: He says they depend on mum or dad to feed, clothe and care for them.

A book author and a father of a toddler
A presenter on Woman's Hour
A scientist who studies how young children sleep
questions.why: Beth says he is the author of a new book and father to his own toddler.

questions.q: What did the little boy Coltan do?
options: He asked an adult to help with his boots
He cried because he couldn't find his gloves anywhere
He told Julie she was doing it wrong
He said out loud that he'd put his boots on wrongly
questions.why: Looking at his boots on the wrong way, he said, “Oh, Coltan did this wrong!”

questions.q: According to Dr Merali, what does self-talk help toddlers do?
options: Learn new words more quickly than other children
Make friends with other children
Feel less stressed in worrying situations
Get their parents' attention
questions.why: He says self-talk is a way to decrease stress in anxiety-provoking situations.

questions.q: How does our self-talk often change as we grow up?
options: It becomes quieter but kinder
It becomes less encouraging and more critical
It stops completely
It becomes more positive, loving and encouraging
questions.why: Neil says as we grow up, our self-talk often becomes less encouraging and more critical.

questions.q: What does Dr Merali advise adults who are angry with themselves?
options: Talk to yourself as if you were a good friend
Stop talking to yourself altogether
Ask a toddler for advice
Write all your negative thoughts down in a diary
questions.why: He suggests thinking about talking to yourself as a good friend instead.
